texts: Surrounds a captive star with a swarm, and eventually a sphere, of collectors.$(br2)Generates power.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 5$() machine.

Freeman Dyson, 1960: a civilisation hungry enough for energy would wrap its star in collectors, and we could spot it by its waste heat. I appear to be that civilisation now.$(br2)This controller is too complex for a crafting grid. Build it on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() - check JEI for the exact parts.

Loading it: a $(item)Stellar Core$() in the first slot. $(item)Dyson Swarm Satellites$() (up to 500) in the second - or leave a $(item)Von Neumann Probe$() there and it builds the swarm by itself. $(item)Dyson Shell Segments$() in the third: 64 close the sphere, but you need 100 satellites before shells can be mounted.

The yield, as I have worked it out:$(br2)Output = base x satellites/50 x (1 + shells/16)$(br2)and doubled again once the sphere is complete. A finished sphere is the brightest thing I have built, and from outside you cannot see it at all.
Takes a star through its whole life - collapse, ignition, giant phase, death - and keeps the elements it forges.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.

Almost every atom heavier than helium in my body was cooked inside a star. This chamber runs that process on a workbench: a gas cloud falls in on itself, fusion lights, the star swells, and it dies. My notes on stellar evolution follow each stage.
Day 77. A star begins as a cloud. I harvest $(fluid)Nebular Gas$() with the Dark Matter Halo Collector and collapse it into a $(item)Protostar$() in the $(item)Nucleosynthesis Chamber$().

Gravity squeezes until the core reaches millions of degrees and hydrogen fuses. I ignite the protostar into a $(item)Stellar Core$(). When a real star runs low on hydrogen its outer layers balloon outward; mine swells into a $(item)Red Giant$(), and I keep its $(item)White Dwarf$() - the bare, glowing core left behind.

White dwarfs forge $(item)Stellar Iron$() - the end of fusion. Iron's nucleus is among the most tightly bound there is; fusing it costs energy instead of releasing it. Dyson shells are made of stellar iron.

A red giant crushed onto stellar iron goes supernova. Its remnant feeds the $(item)r-process$() - rapid neutron capture, nature's way of making gold and everything heavier - and it is needed for every quark star.

Four plasma injectors fire into a coil-wrapped chamber hotter than a hypernova. Burns catalyst plasmas to forge metals whose properties are chosen rather than discovered.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 6$() machine.

A hypernova is the death of a star so massive its explosion outshines an ordinary supernova many times over. This chamber runs hotter.$(br2)This controller is too complex for a crafting grid. Build it on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() - check JEI for the exact parts.

First firing. It has to be bootstrapped with $(fluid)Residual Starlight$(), made from a Stellar Core. Every forging after that burns a catalyst plasma and leaves $(fluid)Dimensional Residue$() behind.

Coil tier sets what it can forge:$(li)tier 3: Hypernova Alloy$(li)tier 4: Hypernova Plasma$(li)tier 5 (Transfinite Coils): Transcendent Metal$(br2)Note to self: upgrade the coils before ordering the plasma, not after.
